evidence.supports: Standard oxygen dissociation curve, not a dynamic hypoxia trajectory
Adult reference magnitudes for FRC, tidal volume, Hb, shunt, dead space, RQ and oxygen demand; not this model's fitted parameters
Blood oxygen content includes Hb-bound and dissolved components; mix contents by flow
Nadler adult blood volume model attribution
Table 1 reproduces the male/female Nadler coefficients, height in metres, weight in kilograms, output in litres
Fixed mL/kg estimation is unsuitable across obesity; no obesity estimator is implemented here

authored_assumptions: Adult circulating model only; low/no-flow and pediatric states are rejected or excluded
Nadler admission restricted to age18..90, height140..210cm, weight40..150kg and BMI18.5..<30; these are prototype bounds, not validated clinical formula boundaries
Blood volume is estimated, not measured; effective arterial/systemic-venous split0.2/0.8 is independent of Nadler
Other physiological parameters do not automatically scale from patient demographics
Cardiac output5L/min, constant Hb, fixed37C and pH7.4; lung capillary equilibrium is instantaneous
Systemic oxygen consumption is lumped in venous blood; no separate organ/tissue pool
Actual demand scales linearly below venous oxygen content2mL/dL; unmet demand is tracked, not interpreted as injury
O2/CO2/inert gas inventories use STPD; lung volume uses BTPS at760mmHg with water vapour47mmHg
CO2 production enters the gas reservoir immediately as RQ times actual oxygen consumption; no blood CO2 buffer or Bohr shift
Inspiratory-gated mixed-gas washout integrates to max(VT-VD,0) per breath; not a lung mechanics or dead-space plug-flow model
Open airway replenishes net gas uptake and relaxes the isobaric gas reservoir toward reference FRC over2s
Closed airway has no gas input/output and its isobaric reservoir contracts; airway pressure and passive reopening mechanics are not predicted
Sensitivity ranges deliberately extend beyond the reference cohort and are not population confidence intervals
